The team note conflicts with the example assertion, so I kept the original approach. Cutting into consecutive blocks of n would give `[['a','b','c'], ['d','e','f'], ...]`, which fails the required assert. The assert expects the i-th sublist to hold every nth element starting at offset i, so the result always has n sublists.

```python
def list_split(lst, n):
    return [lst[i::n] for i in range(n)]
```
